change: Question: Imagine it happened differently. Start with *If I*: I didn't see the sign, so I got a parking fine. Answers (replace the list): "If I had seen the sign, I wouldn't have got a parking fine." / "If I had seen the sign, I wouldn't have gotten a parking fine." / "If I had seen the sign, I wouldn't have got a fine." / "If I had seen the sign, I wouldn't have gotten a fine." / "If I had seen the sign, I wouldn't have been fined." / "If I had noticed the sign, I wouldn't have got a parking fine. :: Correct too: *noticed* = saw. :: Arī pareizi: *noticed* = pamanīju." / "If I had noticed the sign, I wouldn't have got a fine. :: (same note)" (the grader adds the other clause order and the contractions).
reason: Two results (parked / got a fine) leave open how many go into the answer, so readers keep finding combinations after the round-1 additions (reader 2: instruction). One result closes it; this replaces r1-003's additions for that reason.
A gap task with the verbs in brackets needs no instruction line (the app's style); two verbs in brackets for two gaps show that a gap may take more than one word. r1-005's *might / could be* stay.
The reader accepts it; *if I worked* (yes/no pattern for a wh-question) is a real learner mistake and was chosen by r1-006 for error type IND-YESNO.

No instruction line is the app's gap style; the quote is the source being reported. *congratulate* + person + *on* + -ing is a reporting-verb pattern (Murphy Intermediate 62, 133), C1 relabelled B2.2. *for* is not added: *congratulate for* is found in standard use, so it would be a second correct answer.

change: Question: Report it with *advise*: My sister said to me: 'You really should see a doctor about that cough.' Answers: keep only the *advised* answers (*advised me to see* / *advised that I (should) see* / *advised seeing* … about that cough / my cough) and add "My sister advised me to see a doctor about the cough." / "My sister advised me to go to the doctor about that cough." / "My sister advised me to go to the doctor about my cough." Note on *advised that I (should) see* and *advised seeing*: "Correct too; the most common pattern is *advise* + person + *to*: *advised me to see*. :: Arī pareizi; visbiežāk saka *advise* + persona + *to*: *advised me to see*." Why: "*advise* + person + *to* + base verb: *My sister advised me to see a doctor.*"
reason: Both readers: *Say what my sister did* does not ask for a reporting verb, so every paraphrase (*said I should*, *go to the doctor*) is correct and the list never closes; naming the verb keeps the point (the pattern after *advise*) and closes it.

change: Add answers: "Could you tell me why my order hasn't arrived?" / "Could you please tell me why my order hasn't arrived?" / "Could you tell me why my order hasn't arrived, please?" / "Could you tell me why my order hasn't arrived yet?" (same meaning, no note).
reason: Both readers wrote *my order*; a natural, correct choice of the customer, refused.

change: Question: Join with *which*: We visited a museum. It has a collection of old cars. Answers: the same four with *a collection of old cars* (which / that + has / had; keep r1-029's note on *had*).
reason: Both readers: *a museum which has old cars* is not natural; *has a collection of* is what a native says and keeps the A2 relative clause.

change: Add answers: "The app, which helps me learn new words, is free." / "The app, which helps me to learn new words, is free." / "The app, which is free, helps me to learn new words." with note "Correct too: with commas the clause only adds information about the one app. :: Arī pareizi: ar komatiem palīgteikums tikai pievieno informāciju par šo vienu lietotni."
reason: Both clause choices are already accepted (no instruction change needed), but the commas version with *which helps me learn* is correct (reader 1) and refused. Level: a clause inside the subject is A2 in Murphy Essential Grammar (r1-030).
A learning task (role learn): matching by meaning is acceptable, and no two endings can be swapped (people take *who*, things *which*). *travels for fun* is a fair A2 definition.

change: Add answers: "The concert tickets might already be sold out. :: Correct too: *already* adds 'by now'. :: Arī pareizi: *already* = jau." / "The concert might be sold out." (same meaning, no note).
reason: Both readers wrote *might already be*; reader 2 *The concert might be sold out*; both are correct rewrites with *might*, refused.

change: Right cards: *Yes, I'm sure.* -> *Definitely.*; *Yes, perhaps.* -> *Perhaps.*; *No, I'm sure.* -> *Definitely not.*; *Perhaps not.* stays. Pairs: She'll call. = Definitely. | She might call. = Perhaps. | She won't call. = Definitely not. | She might not call. = Perhaps not.
reason: Both readers: *No, I'm sure.* reads as a reply, not a meaning. *Definitely / Perhaps (not)* are clear, and no two can be swapped.

change: Question: Start with *I've decided*: I will go home early. Answers unchanged (the *I've / I have decided* ones fit; the *I decided* ones are harmless).
reason: Both readers: *Make a sentence with decide* leaves the tense open and allows *I will decide to go home early*. The start fixes the tense and leaves the pattern (*decided to go*) to the learner; r1-067's answers stay.
